dedupe_keys.name: carats open data radar flight track data for the fukuoka fir japan civil aviation bureau

description: CARATS Open Data is a large set of real aircraft track data that Japan's Civil Aviation Bureau has provided since February 2015 under CARATS, its long-term plan for the future air traffic system, to encourage research. The Electronic Navigation Research Institute prepares it from air traffic control records. It holds about 820,000 flights of scheduled instrument flights (military and private aircraft excluded) in one week of every odd month from fiscal 2012 to 2016, 30 weeks in all, from en-route radar, Haneda terminal radar from 2013, Haneda aerodrome surface surveillance from 2016 and ADS-C oceanic data from 2015, covering the radar airspace of the Fukuoka flight information region and, from 2015, the whole region. Each CSV row gives time, an anonymised flight number, latitude, longitude, altitude in feet and aircraft type, about every 10 seconds (8 seconds terminal, 1 minute oceanic, 1 second on the airport surface); ENRI checked positions against GPS. Per the 2019 ENRI presentation, data are free on application by e-mail to the CARATS office and sent on disc, for research, education and outreach in air traffic, with no redistribution and acknowledgement in publications. Caveats: the current application page was not found, so the terms and any newer years should be confirmed. The tracks support capacity and arrival-flow simulation and relate to the OpenSky Network and AMELIA catalogued here.
